A.explanation: Too small by a factor of 4, obtained if diameter $50\text{ mm}$ is mistakenly used as radius in $A = \pi r^2$.

B.explanation: About half the correct value, obtained if diameter is used without squaring correctly or if area is doubled.

C.explanation: Volume flow rate divided by nozzle area gives about $25\text{ m s}^{-1}$, matching the mass, time and density data.

D.explanation: About twice the correct value, obtained if radius $25\text{ mm}$ is mistakenly used as diameter in the area calculation.

hints: Notice the $100\text{ kg}$ in $2.0\text{ s}$ with density $1000\text{ kg m}^{-3}$ gives a volume and then a volume per second through the nozzle.
Recall volume flow rate $Q = Av$, so you need the circular area from the $50\text{ mm}$ diameter converted to metres.
Convert $50\text{ mm}$ to $0.050\text{ m}$ and use radius $0.025\text{ m}$ in $A = \pi r^2$ before dividing $Q$ by $A$.
walkthrough: Find the volume of water from density $\rho = m/V$. Rearranged, $V = m/\rho = 100/1000 = 0.10\text{ m}^3$ passing in $2.0\text{ s}$.
Find the volume flow rate $Q = V/t = 0.10/2.0 = 0.050\text{ m}^3\text{ s}^{-1}$.
Find the nozzle cross-sectional area. Diameter $d = 50\text{ mm} = 0.050\text{ m}$, so radius $r = 0.025\text{ m}$ and $A = \pi r^2 = \pi \times (0.025)^2 \approx 1.96 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}^2$.
Use continuity $Q = Av$ to get speed $v = Q/A$. So $v \approx 0.050/(1.96 \times 10^{-3}) \approx 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$ with unit check $\text{m}^3\text{s}^{-1}/\text{m}^2 = \text{m s}^{-1}$.
